biography.ja: マンハイムに生まれ、マンハイム楽派の創始者である父ヨハン・シュターミッツをはじめ、複数の楽団の名手たちに師事した。父の跡を継ぐ形でヴァイオリン・ヴィオラ奏者、作曲家として活動し、弟であり弟子でもあるアントンと共に楽団で演奏することもあった。
biography.en: Born in Mannheim, he studied under his father Johann Stamitz, founder of the Mannheim school, as well as other virtuoso players from the local orchestra. Following in his father's footsteps, he was active as a violinist, violist, and composer, and he sometimes performed together in the orchestra with his younger brother and pupil, Anton.

style.ja: 父が築いたマンハイム楽派の劇的な強弱の変化、いわゆる「マンハイムのロケット」と呼ばれる急激なクレッシェンドなど、当時としては先進的な管弦楽の演奏効果を受け継いだ作風を特徴とする。協奏交響曲という編成を得意とし、複数の独奏楽器を対話させる華やかな作品を数多く残した。
style.en: His style is marked by the dramatic dynamic effects pioneered by the Mannheim school his father built, including the so-called "Mannheim rocket," a sudden sweeping crescendo that was advanced orchestral technique for its time. He excelled at the sinfonia concertante form, leaving many brilliant works featuring dialogue among multiple soloists.

impact.ja: 父が確立したマンハイム楽派の演奏効果は、後にハイドンやモーツァルトのウィーン古典派交響曲にも取り入れられており、彼はその成果を次世代へと伝える継承者としての役割を果たした。マンハイム楽派という一つの流派が、家族を通じて世代を超えて受け継がれていった稀有な例として音楽史に位置づけられる。
impact.en: The orchestral effects of the Mannheim school established by his father were later absorbed into the Viennese Classical symphonies of Haydn and Mozart, and he played the role of a successor who carried that achievement forward into the next generation. He is recorded in music history as a rare example of a school of music, the Mannheim school, being passed down across generations within a single family.

ja: マンハイム楽派創始者の息子
マンハイムのロケットを受け継ぐ作風
ハイドン・モーツァルトへの技法的継承
en: Son of the Mannheim school's founder
Style carrying forward the Mannheim rocket
Technique passed forward to Haydn and Mozart
